options_security_sub.message: Scope, protocol alignment, and known limitations of this extension.

options_security_card1_text.message: Standard TOTP and enhanced codes are all computed locally with WebCrypto. Apart from submitting a code to the account's own fixed URL (and binding confirmation), no external network requests are made, and no analytics, statistics, or remote scripts are included.

options_security_card2_text.message: Secrets are encrypted with AES-GCM before being written to disk; the AES master key is stored in IndexedDB and is non-exportable. Browser extensions cannot access the system keystore, which is the trade-off without a native host. See the security limitations in the README.

options_security_card3_text.message: During QR sign-in, only the registrable domain of the QR code is compared with the registrable domain pinned locally; the submit path always comes from the binding, never from the QR code. With zero candidates the flow stops locally without sending any request.

options_security_card4_text.message: Enhanced accounts do not display codes and offer no copying or auto-fill; they can only submit by QR scan. The submit target comes from the local fixed URL, and the URL in the QR code is never used as the target.

options_security_card5_text.message: Binding QR codes carry no signature. The extension stores only the domain and submit path you confirm at binding time, and all later submissions use that address alone. The login QR code supplies only a domain and a session token, never the submit target.

options_security_card6_text.message: If a backup file (or the password of an encrypted backup) leaks, anyone can generate codes. Enhanced account secrets are exported in JSON backups by default as required; this is a deliberate relaxation of the “no export” limit and is confirmed twice before export.

options_limitation1.message: System biometrics and hardware keystores cannot be used; if the extension context is fully compromised, secrets cannot be protected from reading.

options_limitation2.message: QR content comes from untrusted pages. Even if URL matching passes, a malicious site can display a real server's QR code on its own page and trick the user into submitting (relay phishing). Check the browser address bar and the submit target.

options_limitation3.message: Codes depend on local time; a large clock skew will cause authentication failures.

options_limitation4.message: QR codes inside cross-origin iframes may be unreadable due to browser security policy.

options_limitation5.message: To support fixed-URL submission and binding confirmation, the extension requests host permissions for HTTPS and loopback addresses. It does not read page content unless you explicitly click scan or fill.
